title: Deep learning of salivary-gland biopsies identifies acinar CD8 T-cell infiltration associated with Sjögren disease
summary: A deep-learning model trained on digitized minor salivary-gland biopsy slides from five expert centres and externally validated at a sixth classified focus score and Sjögren disease in a retrospective cohort of 545 participants. Explainable-model analysis identified a histological pattern of CD8-positive T cells around acinar epithelial cells associated with Sjögren disease. External-validation AUROC was 0.89 for disease classification and 0.92 among patients negative for anti-SSA antibodies.
ai_technology: Deep-learning histopathology classifier with Shapley-value interpretation
organization: Scienta Lab; William Harvey Research Institute, Queen Mary University of London; University of Birmingham; National and Kapodistrian University of Athens; Newcastle University; Université Paris-Saclay; participating NECESSITY consortium centres

evidence.tested: A deep-learning model trained on digitized minor salivary-gland biopsy slides from five expert centres and externally validated at a sixth classified focus score and Sjögren disease in a retrospective cohort of 545 participants.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective multicentre cohort; external validation used one held-out expert centre. The authors state further validation is needed. The CD8 acinar-infiltration pattern was associated with disease classification and is not established as causal, pathognomonic, or clinically actionable. The study does not establish improved patient outcomes or replace expert pathology.
evidence.ai_role: The authors trained the deep-learning model on digitalized biopsy slides to classify focus score and Sjögren disease, tested generalization at a held-out centre, and used Shapley-value explanations to identify histological patterns associated with model decisions. The study reports acinar CD8-positive T-cell infiltration as a disease-associated pattern.
